title: Bisect the break
brief:
The app is broken at HEAD and the break is somewhere in the last six commits. Reading every diff would take all afternoon. `git bisect` binary-searches history instead: you mark the tip `bad` and a known-good old commit `good`; git checks out the commit in the MIDDLE; you look at `app.txt` and answer good or bad; repeat. Each answer halves the suspects.

In this repo, broken means `app.txt` contains the line BROKEN.

Start the search with `git bisect start`, mark the tip bad, mark `HEAD~5` good, then answer honestly about each checkout. When git names the first bad commit, Gitsy leaves you standing right on it so you can inspect the culprit.

goals.label: You are standing on the culprit
Exactly four commits are visible from here

hints: git bisect start, git bisect bad, git bisect good HEAD~5.
At each checkout, look at app.txt in the working tree panel. BROKEN line means git bisect bad; no BROKEN line means git bisect good.
Five suspects, so about three answers. Lying to bisect does not break it; it just names the wrong commit.
